about: The epistola of the formulary “6th Sunday after Pentecost” in the 1962 Roman Missal.

seg.tr: Brethren: All of us who were baptized in Christ Jesus were baptized in His death. For we have been buried together with Him through baptism into death, so that, as Christ rose from the dead by the glory of the Father, we too may likewise walk in newness of life. For if we have been planted together in the likeness of His death, we will also be in the likeness of His resurrection, knowing this, that our old man has been crucified together with Him, so that the body of sin may be destroyed, and we may no longer serve sin. For he who has died has been justified from sin. But if we died with Christ, we believe we will also live together with Christ, knowing that Christ, rising from the dead, dies no more; death will no longer rule over Him. For in dying to sin, He died once; but in living, He lives to God. So you also, consider yourselves dead indeed to sin, but living to God, in Christ Jesus our Lord.
